PROJECT 02 / WEB SYSTEM

IPL Auction.

Bring the auction room to the browser.

PROJECT TYPEAcademic prototype
TECHNOLOGIESPython · Flask · PostgreSQL
View source code ↗
IN THIS PROJECTThe problemThe approachSource evidenceLimitations & next steps
01 / CONTEXT

The problem.

An auction has connected state: players, teams, bids, and a finite purse. A browser application makes those relationships tangible and gives participants a shared way to follow the process.

02 / IMPLEMENTATION

The approach.

Model players, teams, and users in PostgreSQL and expose the auction interface through Flask. The repository also includes a player-data scraping script and templates for account and auction screens.

01Player and team records
02Flask auction workflow
03PostgreSQL state
01

Relational auction state

Players, teams, and users have separate database tables. Teams begin with a configured purse and players carry performance and bidding fields.

02

A browser-based workflow

Flask renders the auction screen and account pages. Player records include runs, wickets, batting and bowling averages, and current bids.

03

A deployment-oriented structure

The source includes a Procfile, Python runtime configuration, and a database connection configured through DATABASE_URL.

03 / SHOW THE WORK

04 / HONEST BOUNDARIES

What still needs work.

  • This is presented as an auction application. Predictive valuation and squad optimization are not claimed as implemented features.
  • The reviewed source needs authentication hardening, including password hashing and server-controlled role assignment, before public use.
  • Concurrent bidding behavior and deployment reliability have not been benchmarked here.
NEXT ITERATION

Harden authentication, verify concurrent bidding and purse updates, and document a reproducible demo before adding predictive features.

A useful data application begins with a clear model of the underlying workflow and consistent state.
